questions.q: Why does this capstone recommend organizing the toolkit into purpose-based folders with a README, instead of one flat folder of .sql files?
options: So a DBA can find the right script quickly during an incident, using the README as a plain-language index instead of reading file contents under pressure
Because SQL Server refuses to execute scripts stored in a flat folder
Because git requires at least three subfolders to track a repository
Folder structure has no practical effect on usability
questions.explain: During an actual incident, you want to find the right script fast. A README with one line per script, organized by purpose, is the index a DBA actually reads under pressure.

questions.q: What makes a script's "Last verified" header line trustworthy over time, according to this lesson?
options: Committing an update to that line, with a matching commit message, every time the script is re-tested against a new SQL Server version
Writing the line once when the script is first created and never touching it again
Deleting the line entirely once a script is a year old
The line is purely decorative and has no bearing on trust
questions.explain: Source control turns a Last verified claim into a provable fact — the commit history shows exactly when the script was re-tested against a given version.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a new DBA do with this toolkit on their actual first day in a new role?
options: Run it as-is first to get a baseline, then start adjusting thresholds and exclusion lists to match what's normal on that specific environment
Immediately rewrite every script from scratch before running anything
Never run any script until a manager explicitly approves each one individually
Run only the scripts that modify data, since read-only scripts provide no value on day one
questions.explain: The lesson recommends running the health check as-is for a baseline first, then tuning thresholds like @FullBackupThresholdHours and the benign-wait exclusion list to match the new environment.

questions.q: Which of the following is given as an example of "judgment about safety" that a toolkit walkthrough demonstrates in an interview?
options: Pointing at the @DryRun guard and explaining why it defaults to 1
Reciting the exact syntax of every DMV column from memory
Showing that the script has never been modified since it was written
Demonstrating that the script contains no comments at all
questions.explain: The lesson specifically calls out explaining the @DryRun default as a signal of judgment about blast radius, not just syntax knowledge.

questions.q: Within the SQL Server Database Administrator career path's Job Ready stage, what course does this capstone point to as coming next after T-SQL for Database Administrators?
options: SQL Server Database Administration
Azure Database Administrator
SQL Server Performance Tuning
PowerShell Automation and DevOps for DBAs
questions.explain: The Job Ready stage runs T-SQL Development, then T-SQL for Database Administrators, then SQL Server Database Administration — the course this capstone points to next.
